ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 1, the solid lines are the electric field lines around equal and unlike point charges, and the dashed line is a circle centered on one point charge. Point M is the midpoint of the line connecting the two point charges. If a positive test point charge is moved from point N on the dashed line to point M, how does the magnitude of the electric field force on this charge change?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: observing the attached figure, the point charge on the left is marked “+”, and the point charge on the right is marked “-”; the two are equal and unlike; the solid electric field lines start from the positive charge on the left and point toward the negative charge on the right, indicating that the overall direction of the electric field between the two charges is from left to right. The dashed line is a circular arc centered on the positive charge on the left; point N is at the upper-right position of the dashed circle, and point M is near the midpoint of the line connecting the two charges and is at the right side of the dashed circle. Then reason: the magnitude of the electric field force on the positive test charge is F=qE. Since the charge quantity q of the test charge is unchanged, it is only necessary to judge the change in the magnitude of the resultant electric field strength E. When moving from N to M along the dashed circle, the distance to the positive charge on the left remains unchanged, so the magnitude of the field strength produced by the positive charge on the left at that point remains unchanged; at the same time, that point gradually approaches the negative charge on the right, and the distance to the negative charge decreases, so the field strength produced by the negative charge on the right gradually increases. Moreover, during the process from N to M, the direction of the field strength produced by the positive charge and the direction of the field strength produced by the negative charge become increasingly close to the same direction; at M, both are along the line connecting the two charges to the right. Therefore, the resultant electric field strength gradually increases, and the magnitude of the electric field force on the positive test charge also gradually increases.
